plan.title: Capstone PowerShell 7.4+ block does not enforce the shell version

narratives.Description: The capstone labels its Windows starting-state fence as PowerShell 7.4+ but does not inspect `$PSVersionTable`, so an unsupported shell can begin the final evidence workflow before failing on later behavior. This story copies the established Labs 2 and 5 version guard into the wrapper's first statement and adds focused content regression coverage without changing the Node helper or any other PowerShell route.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Update the Windows Environment fence in `labs/capstone-end-to-end.md` so the PowerShell 7.4 guard is its first statement, before `$ErrorActionPreference` or any stateful operation.
2. Add a focused `labEnvironment` assertion in `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs` for the established Labs 2 and 5 guard expression.
3. Extend `scripts/verify-capstone.test.mjs` with a negative fixture that removes the guard and proves the content check fails, while keeping the helper and unrelated routes outside the diff.
narratives.UserStory: As a Windows capstone learner, I want the PowerShell 7.4 minimum enforced before any setup runs, so that I cannot begin the final evidence workflow in an unsupported shell.
narratives.Traces: Accepted bound remedy on https://github.com/deftai/directive-training/issues/61#issuecomment-5786103216 and confirmed by synthesis comment 5787727332; relieves recorded pain P1.
narratives.Overview:
## Learner context

Independent Windows/PowerShell pilot preparing to complete the full course and capstone.

## Problem

`labs/capstone-end-to-end.md` labels its Windows block **Windows PowerShell 7.4+**, but the block does not test `$PSVersionTable.PSVersion`. It validates Node 22+, paths, and several tool versions, while relying on the heading alone for the shell minimum.

Labs 2 and 5 already demonstrate the stronger pattern:

```powershell
if ($PSVersionTable.PSVersion -lt [version]'7.4') { throw 'PowerShell 7.4 or newer is required' }
```

## Pain experienced

The capstone is the final evidence gate. A learner on Windows PowerShell 5.1 or an older PowerShell 7 can begin creating temporary directories before discovering syntax/runtime differences. A heading is guidance, not the deterministic preflight the course teaches.

## Proposed fix

Add the same explicit PowerShell version assertion as the first statement in the capstone Windows block, before any state is created.

No Directive source or framework internals were consulted.

Census: 0 `blocks-the-design`, 1 `sharpens-framing`, 2 `footnote`. Copying the Labs 2/5 throw into the capstone starting-state fence is the right existing mechanism. Bind it on that fence and on the Windows-start lock that already owns the block.

## 1. Name the starting-state fence and extend the existing Windows-start lock — sharpens-framing

Evidence, measured at `a484f30613f16d1da3c8f7a01edb5d67e562a12e`:

- `labs/capstone-end-to-end.md` uses the heading `### Windows PowerShell 7.4+` at lines 88 and 175. Four `powershell` fences exist (open at 94, 177, 432, 459). Only fence 1 (`Environment and starting-state check`, lines 94–129) calls `New-Item` (117, 119). Its first statement is `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`. None of the four fences contain `$PSVersionTable`.
- Stop 1 P1 cites 88–115. That slice is the preflight through `python --version` (115), still before `New-Item`. Labs 2/5 first-statement throws re-read as written: `labs/02-disposable-initialization.md:155` and `labs/05-projection-drift-recovery.md:67` are `if ($PSVersionTable.PSVersion -lt [version]'7.4') { throw 'PowerShell 7.4 or newer is required' }`.
- `node scripts/verify-capstone.mjs` exits 0 (`Capstone content contract: ok (36 artifacts, 0 missing)`) with that hole still present. `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs` already locks the same `labEnvironment` slice for missing `DIRECTIVE_TRAINING_ROOT`, `$CourseRoot = [IO.Path]::GetFullPath($env:DIRECTIVE_TRAINING_ROOT)`, and a fake clone path (lines 714–736), and already locks the Node 22 wrapper assertion on the lab (750–753). `scripts/verify-capstone.test.mjs` 109–116 is the sibling negative mutation for that Windows-start lock.
- Lab 2 already fail-closes the same throw: `scripts/verify-modules-2-3.mjs:321` on the lab and `:989` on `.github/workflows/modules-2-3-platform-validation.yml` (workflow line 176 places the throw before `$ErrorActionPreference`). `scripts/verify-modules-4-5.mjs` does not lock Lab 5’s throw. `labs/fixtures/capstone-end-to-end/capstone-lab.mjs` has no `$PSVersionTable`. The lab already assigns runtime floors to the wrapper (`labs/capstone-end-to-end.md:55–57`: helper does not assert `process.version`; wrappers check Node before `create`).

Failure mode: the phrase “the capstone Windows block” can harvest the install fence at 177, which runs after `create`. Fence 1 would still mint temp directories on older PowerShell 7. A markdown-only recut of fence 1 also stays green in `verify-capstone.mjs`, so the heading-only hole this issue files can return on the next edit of the same block.

Disposition: Bound-remedy names the first statement of the `Environment and starting-state check` `powershell` fence (opens at line 94), using the Lab 2/5 throw before `$ErrorActionPreference`. Add one `assert.match` on the existing `labEnvironment` slice in `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs` with Lab 2’s regex `/\$PSVersionTable\.PSVersion -lt \[version\]'7\.4'/`, and extend the existing Windows-start negative test in `scripts/verify-capstone.test.mjs`. Keep the check in the wrapper; the helper remains Node.

Road not taken: a `create()` check inside `capstone-lab.mjs` (the lab already puts runtime floors on the wrapper). Repeating the throw on fences 2–4 (Lab 2’s every-fence habit; Lab 5 and this starting-state pain are first-fence).

Steelmanning markdown-only: Lab 5 already publishes this throw with no modules-4-5 lock, and the issue names Labs 2/5 as the pattern. Flip this heading off the verifier if the successor map records markdown-only identity and leaves the `labEnvironment` lock out of harvest, matching Lab 5.

## 2. Windows PowerShell 5.1 directory-creation claim is unverified here — footnote

Issue-body pain says a 5.1 or older PowerShell 7 learner can begin creating temporary directories. At this SHA, fence 1 calls `[IO.Path]::IsPathFullyQualified` at line 100 and first `New-Item` at 117. This seat did not execute Windows PowerShell 5.1. If that host’s `Path` surface lacks `IsPathFullyQualified`, 5.1 stops before `New-Item` with a method error. PowerShell 7 includes that member; `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true` on 7.0/7.1 is an ordinary assignment, then version prints, then `New-Item`. The older-7 half of the pain holds. The recut still earns the Labs 2/5 throw message. Treat 5.1 directory creation as unverified on the successor map.

## 3. Other 7.4+ headed routes stay outside this recut — footnote

Lab 7 (`labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:412`), Lab 10, Lab 11, and `labs/README.md:93–107` head native Windows routes `PowerShell 7.4+` and also omit `$PSVersionTable`. Capstone fences 2–4 omit it as well and do not create the starting-state directories. Lab 2 repeats the throw on seven fences; Lab 5 only on the first. This issue’s closed identity is the capstone starting-state fence. Those other surfaces are leftover catalog, not this Bound-remedy.

Injection / swarm lens: not triggered. The target is a taught wrapper assertion plus an existing content-contract regex.
